v1.739.1.note: Newest release at the time; used instead of v1.731.1 because its target descends from main 3142c5a.

uninstall.route: Update.exe --uninstall on a hidden desktop; finished in under 10 s
uninstall.leftBehind: the install root folder itself still held Update.exe and a one-byte .dead marker (Squirrel's pending-removal marker); nothing else
uninstall.shortcuts: desktop shortcut and Start menu shortcut both removed
uninstall.squirrelRunValue: the app's own startup Run value removed; an unrelated pre-existing verification Run value pointing at another build was left alone
uninstall.nativeMessagingKeys: the Chrome and Edge keys for this app were removed by the uninstall hook; other apps' keys were untouched
uninstall.hostManifest: the manifest inside the owner profile's native-messaging folder was removed by the hook
uninstall.hostManifestNotRemoved: before the test both keys pointed at a manifest inside the isolated test profile (written by earlier test runs with that profile); that file was not touched by the uninstall and still existed afterwards
uninstall.ownerProfile: kept: 71 of 72 files remained (the only missing file was the host manifest the hook removes); one shader-cache index file changed because the uninstall hook runs the app

reinstall.autoLaunch: Setup launched the app by itself on the owner profile; launch confirmed (window and process); quit through Help > Quit, exited within 2 s
reinstall.nativeMessagingKeys: both keys back, now pointing at the manifest in the owner profile
reinstall.manifestPath: the manifest's host path points into app-1.739.1
reinstall.shortcuts: desktop and Start menu shortcuts back, targeting the install-root stub
reinstall.runValue: Squirrel startup Run value back, pointing into app-1.739.1

B_rollback.whatSquirrelDid: Setup.exe of the OLDER v1.729.1 over the installed 1.739.1 did not refuse and did not keep the newer one: its log says the install path already exists and it 'burns it to the ground', then does a first-run install. The older version became the only and current version (app-1.739.1 was deleted).
B_rollback.launch: autolaunched on the owner profile; confirmed by window and process; quit through Help > Quit
B_rollback.selfHeal: registry keys, host manifest path, shortcuts, Uninstall entry (1.729.1) and Run value all pointed into app-1.729.1 right after the install
B_rollback.driveCheck: the 1.729.1 app (user agent 1.729.1) created and mounted a throwaway vault in an isolated test profile, a neutral file written to the mounted drive appeared in the file list; vault locked and its folder deleted
B_rollback.sideEffect: running the 1.729.1 app against the isolated test profile repointed the two native messaging keys at that profile's manifest (again), whose host path pointed into app-1.729.1
B_rollback.updateBack: Setup.exe of v1.739.1 over 1.729.1 behaved the same way: install root rebuilt, app-1.739.1 only; keys, manifest path, shortcuts, Uninstall entry and Run value all pointed to 1.739.1 and the keys point at the owner profile manifest again; launch confirmed, quit through Help > Quit

added: update-staging folder with ready.json and a v1.739.1 package (the app's own updater staging)
owner_profile_final_compare.changedContent: browser cache, storage and log files (GPU, shader, Dawn, Session Storage, Local Storage leveldb, Network state, DIPS) and the host manifest (now names app-1.739.1); these change whenever the app runs

problems: The uninstall leaves the install root folder with Update.exe and a .dead marker behind.
The uninstall does not remove a host manifest that sits in a different profile folder (only the owner profile one), so earlier isolated-profile runs left a manifest behind.
Every Setup.exe run auto-launches the app on the owner profile; those launches change cache files and the updater staged a package there.
Running a different version against an isolated profile rewrites the shared registry keys to that profile's manifest; a later install or launch on the owner profile heals them.
process_cleanup: zero app, Update.exe and java processes at the end; helper password process stopped
